contests.title: Measure A — County Charter Amendments
contests.shortTitle: Measure A
contests.summary: Official ballot question: A TRANSPARENT, ACCOUNTABLE, MODERN COUNTY GOVERNMENT Shall the San Diego County Charter be amended to establish an Independent Ethics Commission, Independent Budget Analyst, Independent Program Auditor, confirmation of certain senior County leaders, and optional Board of Supervisors appointment of the Public Defender; increase term limits from two to three terms for the Board of Supervisors members; require public disclosure of spending and performance data; clarify non-interference provisions; and update terminology and structure?
contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.shortTitle: Measure B
contests.summary: Official ballot question: MEASURE TO FUND SAN DIEGO COUNTY HEALTH & SAFETY SERVICES To clean-up sewage pollution in Tijuana River Valley, improve wildfire prevention, emergency response, access to healthcare, food assistance, childhood development services, and authorized administrative expenses; shall the measure authorizing a half-cent sales tax raising an estimated $400,000,000 to $450,000,000 annually, requiring citizen oversight, public spending disclosure, and independent annual audits, and lasting until ended by voters, be adopted?
contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.summary: Official ballot question: To preserve the City’s ability to continue receiving state infrastructure funding for public works projects, shall the Oceanside City Charter be amended to conform to state laws and best practices regarding prevailing wage and fair competition, including the use of project labor agreements for City public works with mandatory provisions for taxpayer protections, transparency, and accountability in the contracting process, by amending Sections 301, 302, and 303 of the Oceanside City Charter?
contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.title: Measure S — Oceanside Sales Tax
contests.shortTitle: Measure S
contests.summary: Official ballot question: To provide locally-controlled funding for Oceanside services and infrastructure, such as keeping streets, sidewalks, parks, and public facilities safe, clean, and well-maintained; fixing potholes; improving traffic; restoring/protecting local beaches; modernizing public safety/emergency facilities to improve 911 emergency response/community safety; and repairing aging infrastructure, shall City of Oceanside’s ordinance establishing a 1/2 cent sales tax be adopted, providing $20,000,000 annually for general government use for 10 years, with independent audits and citizen oversight?
contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.title: Measure Y — Santee Sales Tax
contests.shortTitle: Measure Y
contests.summary: Official ballot question: To provide funding for City of Santee services and infrastructure, such as fixing streets and potholes; keeping streets, sidewalks, parks and public facilities safe, clean, and well-maintained; repairing/ replacing aging infrastructure and stormdrains; local traffic management; fire protection, paramedic, crime prevention, and 911 emergency response, shall City of Santee’s measure establishing a one cent sales tax be adopted, providing approximately $14,000,000 annually for city services for 10 years, with independent audits, citizens’ committee oversight, and all funds locally controlled?
contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.title: Measure C — Solana Beach Hotel Tax

contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.title: Measure K — Fallbrook Union Elementary School Bonds
contests.shortTitle: Measure K
contests.summary: Official ballot question: To update local elementary and middle schools without increasing tax rates; replace failing roofs, plumbing and electrical systems; improve school safety; construct/repair/acquire classrooms, labs, facilities, equipment, and sites; and qualify for State matching funds; shall Fallbrook Union Elementary School District’s measure be adopted, authorizing $76,000,000 in bonds at legal rates, levying a projected $30 per $100,000 assessed value while bonds are outstanding, generating $5,000,000 annually, with public oversight, audits, no funds for administrators, all funds staying local?
contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.title: Measure P — Ramona Municipal Water District Expenditure Rules
contests.shortTitle: Measure P
contests.summary: Official ballot question: AMENDMENT OF PROPOSITION ‘NN’ TO MODERNIZE THE ORDINANCE. Shall the voters of the Ramona Municipal Water District adopt a measure amending Proposition ‘NN’ by (1) exempting grant funding and donations from the calculation of authorized expenditure limit; (2) increasing the expenditure limit for new projects from $1,000,000 to $10,000,000 where no debt is incurred; and (3) establishing annual adjustments to the expenditure limit based on the San Diego Area Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 2028?
contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.

contests.title: Measure Q — Harris Annex Road Parcel Tax
contests.shortTitle: Measure Q
contests.summary: Official ballot question: Shall the County of San Diego, beginning Fiscal Year 2027-28 and annually thereafter, levy a special tax of up to $1,000 per developed / $375 per undeveloped parcel within Permanent Road Division No. 1000, Zone No. 9B – Harris Annex, replacing the existing assessment? The tax may be adjusted by up to 5% annually based on the Los Angeles Construction Cost Index or a comparable Southern California index and remain until modified or dissolved by law.
contests.yes: Adopt the measure described in the official ballot question.
